title: Continuous preemptive batch scheduler with KV-throttle-aware sizing for streaming chat
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a continuous, preemptive batch scheduler for streaming chat completions that sizes micro-batches based on KV cache pressure, per-session soft-deadlines, and GPU slab headroom. The scheduler should reduce P99 latency regressions caused by naive coalescing while preserving throughput gains from batching and maintaining stable GPU memory usage.

Background: Current continuous batching aggregates streaming requests aggressively which increases throughput but causes KV cache churn and occasional P99 spikes when long sessions or KV-heavy prompts force large KV allocations. We observed these spikes primarily when streaming clients send frequent small turns that get coalesced into large multi-session batches without respecting per-session deadline constraints or KV cache occupancy.

Key heuristics to implement in this ticket:
- Soft-deadline windows: maintain a short per-request soft-deadline (default 60ms) that guarantees the request will not be delayed beyond the window unless preempted for safety.
- KV-throttle-aware sizing: consult a per-GPU KV-occupancy estimator and reduce maximum batch size when KV usage exceeds a configurable threshold to avoid OOMs and excessive compaction.
- Preemptive microflush: if a high-priority request arrives or a session hits its TTL for tokens, preempt currently-accumulating low-priority requests and flush a micro-batch immediately.
- Deficit-based fairness: use a deficit counter per session to prevent starvation while still allowing short-turn coalescing for low-latency clients.
- Slab reservation fallback: reserve a small number of tokens worth of GPU slab for unpredictable KV spikes; if reservation exceeded, route to fallback model-variant or burst pool.
- Streaming chunk alignment: coalesce tokens into GPU-friendly chunk sizes while preserving token-level streaming semantics (order and partial outputs).

Trade-offs discussed:
- Stronger batching increases throughput but risks KV churn and latency spikes; the heuristics bias toward latency SLOs first for streaming chat endpoints.
- Reservation reduces peak throughput but prevents rare, high-cost OOM events and expensive compactions.
- Preemption increases small-batch overhead but substantially improves P99 latency for interactive sessions.

Progress summary:
- Design doc drafted and reviewed (see attachments).
- Simulation harness added to compare baseline vs heuristics using production-like trace sampled from streaming-chat traffic.
- Initial implementation of soft-deadline + KV occupancy sampling in scheduler core (feature branch linked).
- Early sim results: P99 latency down ~18% on sampled traces; average throughput drop ~4% when slab reservation is enabled.

Acceptance criteria:
1) No regression in median latency; P95 and P99 for streaming chat should improve or remain neutral compared to baseline.
2) No increase in GPU OOM rate in Canary.
3) End-to-end correctness: streaming tokens are emitted in-order and partial flush semantics match contract.
4) Config knobs for soft-deadline, kv-threshold, slab-reserve, and preemption enabled by feature-flag.

Next steps:
- Finish unit tests around preemption and fairness counters.
- Run Canary on dedicated cluster for 72h with shadow traffic and monitor OOMs, compactions, and SLO metrics.
- Iterate on defaults based on Canary metrics and customer playback.

Longer-term: evaluate combining this scheduler with model-variant routing (quantized fallback) to further mitigate slab pressure for high-KV workloads.
